title: Detect damaged package records before updating
head: a886c18d3ae6
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
outcome: one medium finding (stop message gives no working repair; plain reinstall fails on flagged records, reproduced) plus two lesser findings (archlinux-keyring record damaged before the check runs; only first damaged record reported), both reproduced, and three optional notes

leads.summary: The repair guard runs after other pacman transactions in the update and channel-change paths
leads.consequence: With an already damaged, otherwise unrelated local entry, omarchy-update-keyring can reinstall archlinux-keyring via sudo pacman -Sy before the guard examines the database. In the channel command, omarchy-refresh-pacman runs -Syyuu and the package switch runs before omarchy-update -y. The proposed check therefore cannot promise to stop package changes before a transaction on these paths, and its failure can arrive after system mutation; a retry repeats those earlier steps. Put a shared preflight before the first transaction if that guarantee is intended.
leads.triage: keyring part already in Opus final (F2), corroboration; channel-set and reinstall-pkgs paths are outside omarchy update and #11316 (Opus final notes them), not published

leads.summary: A nonempty but invalid description is allowed through
leads.consequence: For a partial write with a nonempty desc containing neither %NAME% nor %VERSION%, -s succeeds, so the script starts -Syu. Pacman 7.1.0 initializes name/version from the directory and does not reject missing sections in its desc reader; -Dk only checks file presence. The damaged installed entry therefore remains while the update can finish. Validate required sections or parse metadata, not only file size.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus (opus/followup-1.md): confirmed the check passes it, but realism low (single 4 KiB stdio write, only pacman -D rewrites of 7 large records), plain reinstall or next upgrade fixes it; kept as private limit. Follow-up surfaced cut-short files list as the more plausible undetected shape, published as optional limit note.

leads.summary: A symlink to a directory is incorrectly treated as an installed package record
leads.consequence: On filesystems exposing DT_LNK, pacman/libalpm skips symlinks while enumerating local package records. Bash's glob with */ follows a symlink to a directory, and -d succeeds: a harmless symlink to a saved directory with no desc/files now stops every Omarchy system update with 'Damaged package database record' until removed. Restrict the scan to real directory entries, as pacman does on these filesystems.
leads.triage: dropped: contrived (requires a user-placed symlink in pacman's local db), conditional on d_type

leads.summary: Open PR #9070 conflicts in the update script and both edited conflict tests
leads.consequence: #9070's intentionally different upgrade path removes the conflict recovery helper and changes -Syu to fixed privileged binaries. The three-way merge with the exact common ancestor leaves two conflict blocks in the script and three in each edited test. GitHub currently marks #9070 CONFLICTING against its base. Both cannot be merged automatically; resolving by taking the other PR's script without retaining this guard drops the detection entirely. The #9070 test stubs also need conscious reconciliation with this PR's pacman-conf fixture. No merged test result is asserted since the source has conflict markers.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator (gh pr view 9070: OPEN, CONFLICTING) and by Opus self-check (rewritten script has no record check; both conflict tests execute the real script); published as optional note

leads.summary: The new database test cannot detect a scan that stops after the first record
leads.consequence: All damage cases reuse exactly one package directory. A plausible broken loop with an unconditional break after testing that directory still passes every new assertion; when a valid first record precedes a damaged second, it upgrades. Add a two-record fixture with the first valid and the later record broken to protect the all-installed-packages requirement.
leads.triage: factual, confirmed by reading test (single example-1.0-1 record); merged into Opus F3 (only first record reported), noted in that finding's text

limits: No real host pacman/config/database was read or invoked. Sandbox runs use stub transactions, and claims about pacman's parser and directory scan are based on pinned pacman 7.1.0 source plus current upstream. The #9070 merged code has unresolved textual conflicts, so combined runtime tests are not meaningful.

flags.claim: Outcome: 'the reinstall its message asks for fails on them'; heading '"Reinstall it" fails on the records the check flags'
flags.why: The message asks to restore the entry AND reinstall (bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs:19). Reinstall after restoring works: --dbonly then -S on the emptied shape (plan5 reproducer section 3; plan3 E-14/E-15), rm -r then --dbonly then -S on the missing shape (plan3 M-12..M-14). What fails is a plain reinstall; the defect is that the message gives no command for the restore step.
flags.fix: The check catches the #11316 records, but its message gives no way to restore them, a plain reinstall fails on them, and every later `omarchy update` stops at the check.

flags.claim: For a package that no repository has, `pacman -U --dbonly <file>` followed by `pacman -U <file>` repaired the record the same way in testing.
flags.why: The two -U commands alone repaired only the emptied shape (plan3 FOREIGN-09/10). For desc/files missing, rm -r was run first (plan4 lab-foreign-rm/dbonly/reinstall); without it the same _alpm_pkg_dup failure applies (sync.c:679, package.c:612-618; source inference, not run for -U). The sentence sits in the Reproducer block but the reproducer does not show it.
flags.fix: For a package that no repository has, the same sequence worked with `pacman -U --dbonly <file>` and `pacman -U <file>` in place of the two `pacman -S` commands.

flags.why: repo-add creates/removes its own temp dir under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} (/usr/bin/repo-add:618, :585, :626); in the keyring reproducer the real omarchy-update-system-pkgs makes its mktemp error report in /tmp (bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs:34-35). Both removed; 'never touches the system database' remains correct. Wording originated in my reproducer md files.
flags.fix: writes only to temporary files and directories that are removed on exit

flags.why: The keyring script is a demonstration, script exit 0 (plan7 stdout 'keyring-order exit=0'); both scenarios show the update stopping (exit=1). The gap is the missing guidance, not a failing assertion.
flags.fix: Reproducer (at a886c18) / Reproducer (shows the gap at a886c18)

flags.claim: Open #9070 rewrites the top of `bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs` and both conflict tests, so whichever lands second needs to carry this check and the stubs over.
flags.why: Verified today via read-only gh api: #9070 open, mergeable=false, head f9a99820; it replaces everything below the header (hunk -5,35 +5,38 of a 39-line file, +27 -24), with no record check; both its conflict tests execute the real script (update-file-conflict-test.sh:73, update-package-conflict-test.sh:94,101). 'the top' undersells it.

## Automated AI review > **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review. **Outcome:** The new stop message gives no working repair for the records it catches, so every later `omarchy update` stops at the check. ### The stop message gives no working repair The message does not say how to restore the entry. With `desc` and `files` emptied, a plain `pacman -S ` fails with "exists in filesystem" for every file the package owns, because the empty file list makes each one a conflict. With them missing, `pacman -S`, `-S --dbonly` and `-S --overwrite '*'` all fail with "invalid or corrupted package" until the record directory is removed. **Impact:** a user who cannot work out the repair gets no package updates through `omarchy update`. **Suggested change:** print the sequence that worked in testing for each damaged record: `sudo rm -r `, `sudo pacman -S --dbonly `, then `sudo pacman -S `.
Reproducer (pacman 7.1.0, throwaway root) For a package that no repository has, the same sequence worked in testing with `pacman -U --dbonly ` and `pacman -U ` in place of the two `pacman -S` commands. What the stop message ("Restore this package's database entry and reinstall it before retrying omarchy update.") takes in practice, on a throwaway pacman root. It needs `pacman`, `fakeroot`, `bsdtar` and `repo-add`, writes only to temporary files and directories that are removed on exit, and never touches the system database. Run with `bash repro-repair-guidance.sh`. Reviewed head: a886c18d3ae67f08c0c6320aaec3457b1bef69af. Run with pacman v7.1.0 (libalpm v16.0.1) and fakeroot 1.37.2. ```bash #!/bin/bash # What "restore this package's database entry and reinstall it" takes, on a # throwaway pacman root. Needs pacman, fakeroot, bsdtar and repo-add; writes only # inside a temporary directory and never touches the system database. set -u lab=$(mktemp -d) trap 'rm -rf "$lab"' EXIT mkdir -p "$lab"/{root,db,cache,gpg,hooks,log,repo} cat >"$lab/pacman.conf" <"$lab/fakeroot.state" pm() { fakeroot -i "$lab/fakeroot.state" -s "$lab/fakeroot.state" -- \ pacman --config "$lab/pacman.conf" --noconfirm "$@" } show() { printf '$ pacman' printf ' %q' "$@" echo pm "$@" 2>&1 | grep -E '^(error|demo:|No database errors|reinstalling|installing)' echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}" } # A package "demo" with two files, in a local repository. pkg=$lab/build mkdir -p "$pkg/usr/share/demo" yes payload | head -c 65536 >"$pkg/usr/share/demo/snapshot.bin" echo notes >"$pkg/usr/share/demo/notes.txt" cat >"$pkg/.PKGINFO" </dev/null 2>&1 && pm -S demo >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "setup failed"; exit 1; } record=$lab/db/local/demo-1.0-1 echo "## 1. The #11316 shape: empty desc and files, truncated payload" : >"$record/desc" : >"$record/files" : >"$lab/root/usr/share/demo/snapshot.bin" show -Dk echo echo "## 2. Reinstalling it, as the message says" show -S demo echo echo "## 3. Rewriting the record first, then reinstalling" show -S --dbonly demo show -S demo echo "snapshot.bin is $(stat -c %s "$lab/root/usr/share/demo/snapshot.bin") bytes again" echo echo "## 4. desc and files missing (interrupted before pacman wrote them)" rm "$record/desc" "$record/files" show -S --dbonly demo show -S --overwrite '*' demo echo echo "## 5. Removing the record, then rewriting it and reinstalling" echo "\$ rm -r $record" rm -r "$record" show -S --dbonly demo show -S demo show -Dk ``` Actual output: ```text ## 1. The #11316 shape: empty desc and files, truncated payload $ pacman -Dk No database errors have been found! exit=0 ## 2. Reinstalling it, as the message says $ pacman -S demo error: failed to commit transaction (conflicting files) demo: /tmp/tmp.PkqUccV3lo/root/usr/share/demo/notes.txt exists in filesystem demo: /tmp/tmp.PkqUccV3lo/root/usr/share/demo/snapshot.bin exists in filesystem exit=1 ## 3. Rewriting the record first, then reinstalling $ pacman -S --dbonly demo reinstalling demo... exit=0 $ pacman -S demo reinstalling demo... exit=0 snapshot.bin is 65536 bytes again ## 4. desc and files missing (interrupted before pacman wrote them) $ pacman -S --dbonly demo error: could not open file /tmp/tmp.PkqUccV3lo/db/local/demo-1.0-1/desc: No such file or directory error: failed to prepare transaction (invalid or corrupted package) exit=1 $ pacman -S --overwrite \* demo error: could not open file /tmp/tmp.PkqUccV3lo/db/local/demo-1.0-1/desc: No such file or directory error: failed to prepare transaction (invalid or corrupted package) exit=1 ## 5. Removing the record, then rewriting it and reinstalling $ rm -r /tmp/tmp.PkqUccV3lo/db/local/demo-1.0-1 $ pacman -S --dbonly demo installing demo... exit=0 $ pacman -S demo reinstalling demo... exit=0 $ pacman -Dk No database errors have been found! exit=0 ``` Exit status of the script: 0 (stderr empty). Sections 2 and 4 are the literal "reinstall it" and the obvious variants; sections 3 and 5 are what works.
More findings: a damaged archlinux-keyring record never reaches the check `omarchy update` runs `omarchy-update-keyring`, which reinstalls `archlinux-keyring` on every run, before `omarchy-update-system-pkgs`. If that record is the damaged one, the update stops with pacman's raw "exists in filesystem" or "invalid or corrupted package" error and the new guidance never appears. The merge-base behaves the same, so this is a gap rather than a regression. **Impact:** the one record this flow rewrites on every run gets no repair guidance. **Suggested change:** run the record check before `omarchy-update-keyring`, for example from a small helper that `bin/omarchy-update` calls ahead of the keyring step. **Reproducer (shows the gap at a886c18):** Runs `bin/omarchy-update -y` from an Omarchy checkout against a throwaway pacman root, with `omarchy-update-keyring` and `omarchy-update-system-pkgs` real and every other step stubbed (`sudo` and `pacman-key` are stubs too). It needs `pacman`, `fakeroot`, `bsdtar` and `repo-add`, and writes only to temporary files and directories that are removed on exit. Run `bash repro-keyring-order.sh /path/to/omarchy` with the checkout at the reviewed head a886c18d3ae67f08c0c6320aaec3457b1bef69af. pacman v7.1.0. ```bash #!/bin/bash # Usage: bash repro-keyring-order.sh # Runs that checkout's bin/omarchy-update -y against a throwaway pacman root, # with omarchy-update-keyring and omarchy-update-system-pkgs real and the other # steps stubbed. Needs pacman, fakeroot, bsdtar and repo-add. Writes only inside # a temporary directory; sudo and pacman-key are stubs. set -u repo=$(cd "${1:?usage: repro-keyring-order.sh }" && pwd) lab=$(mktemp -d) trap 'rm -rf "$lab"' EXIT mkdir -p "$lab"/{root,db,cache,gpg,hooks,log,repo,build,stubs} cat >"$lab/pacman.conf" <"$lab/fakeroot.state" for spec in archlinux-keyring:usr/share/pacman/keyrings/archlinux.gpg \ omarchy-keyring:usr/share/pacman/keyrings/omarchy.gpg demo:usr/share/demo/data.bin; do name=${spec%%:*} file=${spec#*:} dir=$lab/build/${spec%%:*} mkdir -p "$dir/$(dirname "$file")" echo "$name" >"$dir/$file" printf 'pkgname = %s\npkgver = 1.0-1\npkgdesc = lab\nbuilddate = 1700000000\npackager = lab\nsize = 1\narch = any\n' "$name" >"$dir/.PKGINFO" (cd "$dir" && bsdtar -czf "$lab/repo/$name-1.0-1-any.pkg.tar.gz" --uid 0 --gid 0 .PKGINFO usr) done repo-add -q "$lab/repo/lab.db.tar.gz" "$lab"/repo/*.pkg.tar.gz cat >"$lab/stubs/pacman" <"$lab/stubs/pacman-conf" <"$lab/stubs/sudo" printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$lab/stubs/pacman-key" printf '#!/bin/bash\nwhile [[ $1 == -* ]]; do shift; done\nexec "$@"\n' >"$lab/stubs/systemd-run" for step in omarchy-update-lock omarchy-update-requires-free-space omarchy-update-pkg-prune \ omarchy-snapshot omarchy-update-stay-awake omarchy-update-dev omarchy-migrate omarchy-hook \ omarchy-update-aur-pkgs omarchy-update-mise omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs \ omarchy-update-analyze-logs omarchy-update-status omarchy-update-restart; do printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$lab/stubs/$step" done chmod +x "$lab"/stubs/* export PATH="$lab/stubs:$repo/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" reset_lab() { rm -rf "$lab"/{root,db,cache}/* "$lab/fakeroot.state" : >"$lab/fakeroot.state" pacman --noconfirm -Sy >/dev/null 2>&1 && pacman --noconfirm -S archlinux-keyring omarchy-keyring demo >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "setup failed"; exit 1; } } update() { OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOGGED=1 bash "$repo/bin/omarchy-update" -y 2>&1 "$lab/db/local/demo-1.0-1/desc" : >"$lab/db/local/demo-1.0-1/files" update echo echo "## archlinux-keyring's record emptied: the keyring step stops first" reset_lab : >"$lab/db/local/archlinux-keyring-1.0-1/desc" : >"$lab/db/local/archlinux-keyring-1.0-1/files" update ``` Actual output (stderr empty, script exit status 0): ```text ## demo's record emptied: the new check reports it Update Arch signing keys Keys are correct Damaged package database record: /tmp/tmp.609CC2dfCR/db/local/demo-1.0-1/ Restore this package's database entry and reinstall it before retrying omarchy update. Something went wrong during the update! Please review the output above carefully, correct the error, and retry the update. If you need assistance, get help from the community at https://omarchy.org/discord exit=1 ## archlinux-keyring's record emptied: the keyring step stops first Update Arch signing keys error: failed to commit transaction (conflicting files) archlinux-keyring: /tmp/tmp.609CC2dfCR/root/usr/share/pacman/keyrings/archlinux.gpg exists in filesystem Something went wrong during the update! Please review the output above carefully, correct the error, and retry the update. If you need assistance, get help from the community at https://omarchy.org/discord exit=1 ``` The same keyring-step failure happens at the merge-base, so this is a gap in where the new check runs, not a regression.
More findings: only the first damaged record is reported The `exit 1` inside the loop stops at the first hit. **Impact:** when one interruption damages several records, each extra one costs another full `omarchy update` run (confirmation, cache prune, snapshot, keyring step) to find. The new test has one record, so it cannot catch this. **Suggested change:** collect every damaged record, print the repair for each, and exit after the loop. **Reproducer (fails at a886c18):** A test in the style of `test/shell.d/update-package-database-test.sh`. Save it as `test/shell.d/update-package-database-all-records-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/update-package-database-all-records-test.sh` from the repository root. It fails at the reviewed head a886c18d3ae67f08c0c6320aaec3457b1bef69af because the check exits at the first damaged record. ```bash #!/bin/bash set -euo pipefail source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh" # Two records damaged by the same interruption: one run should name both, or # every repair costs another full omarchy update (snapshot included) to find # the next one. test_tmp=$(mktemp -d) trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT mkdir -p "$test_tmp/bin" export TEST_DATABASE="$test_tmp/database" for record in first-1.0-1 second-1.0-1; do mkdir -p "$TEST_DATABASE/local/$record" : >"$TEST_DATABASE/local/$record/desc" : >"$TEST_DATABASE/local/$record/files" done cat >"$test_tmp/bin/pacman-conf" <<'STUB' #!/bin/bash printf '%s\n' "$TEST_DATABASE" STUB cat >"$test_tmp/bin/omarchy-update-pacman" <<'STUB' #!/bin/bash exit 0 STUB chmod +x "$test_tmp/bin/"* export PATH="$test_tmp/bin:$PATH" if bash "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs" >"$test_tmp/output" 2>&1; then fail "damaged records stop the update" fi cat "$test_tmp/output" grep -Fq "first-1.0-1/" "$test_tmp/output" || fail "the first damaged record is named" grep -Fq "second-1.0-1/" "$test_tmp/output" || fail "every damaged record is named in one run" pass "every damaged record is named in one run" ``` Actual output at the reviewed head (stdout, then stderr; exit status 1): ```text Damaged package database record: /tmp/tmp.1mecVHbarj/database/local/first-1.0-1/ Restore this package's database entry and reinstall it before retrying omarchy update. not ok - every damaged record is named in one run ```
Details **Verified** (sandbox, pacman 7.1.0): - On the #11316 shape, `pacman -Dk` prints "No database errors have been found!" and the merge-base script's `pacman -Syu` completes; the head script stops before any pacman call on both the automatic and the interactive conflict path. - Healthy records always have a non-empty `desc` and a `files` file, which is 0 bytes for a package that owns no files, so the rule does not block healthy systems. - The new test fails against the merge-base script, and the `pacman-conf` stubs added to the two conflict tests keep them off the host database. **Optional notes:** - Omarchy's default `pacman-conf DBPath` is `/var/lib/pacman/`, so the message prints `/var/lib/pacman//local/-/`; `database=${database%/}` removes the double slash. - Not detected, as a limit: a record whose `files` list is cut short or emptied while `desc` survives passes the check, and a plain reinstall of it then fails with file conflicts. - Open #9070 rewrites `bin/omarchy-update-system-pkgs` and both conflict tests, so whichever lands second needs to carry this check and the stubs over.
